instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Warmth with a Countdown
cards.instruction: Perform increasing warmth with increasingly final language, as though every act of care might also be a goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my good teacup. I'll wrap it for you; I want you to have something from our afternoons here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm only moving two streets away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll put the saucer in as well. You can set a proper place for yourself when these afternoons are over.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can still have tea together, can't we?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. You may bring it back whenever you like. Now choose the biscuit you want packed with it; I won't have our last tea in this room end with you going hungry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take the sandwiches I've packed. Eat one before the bus leaves; I won't have you setting off hungry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm only going to the next town for the afternoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then save the other for coming back. I've cut the crusts off both, so even the end of your journey will be kind to you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're talking as if this is goodbye for good.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let me send you off properly. Come here and let me straighten your scarf. I want you to remember me doing this, not waving after you when you're already too far away to hear.

cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Everything Has Two Prices
cards.instruction: Price every offer twice: once in practical terms and again through an emotional cost that grows when the offer returns.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. The lift costs petrol and a proper conversation about why you stopped calling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pay for petrol.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Good. That gets the car moving, not us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we discuss it another day?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then today costs petrol and another postponed conversation. The second price is rising.

beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. You can borrow the dress for ten pounds and an acknowledgment that you mocked it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's twenty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Money covers fabric. It doesn't cover wearing my bad taste proudly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. It's beautiful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Now say which part of my judgement improved since yesterday.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Agree to the Exact Words
cards.instruction: Agree to the exact wording, then use later callbacks to narrow what those words can obligate you to do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I said I'd carry one box. That warehouse isn't the box.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You promised to help me move.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. With one box. We admired how manageable the sentence was.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Make it the biggest one, then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. The word 'one' has retained its dignity.

beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I agreed to watch your dog today.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An enduring feeling, not a calendar extension.
